transcript.text: Could a sum made from 1, 1/3, 1/7, 1/15, … be a fraction? I explain a condition from Erdős that rules this out for certain selections; the full question is still open.

films.detail: Start with 1, 1/3, 1/7, 1/15, ... and choose infinitely many of those terms. Could their total be a fraction? I try to explain one case of Erdős #257 through examples, then show where the argument appears in the paper and its computer-checked proof. The condition is that adding 1 divided by each chosen position in the original list gives a finite total. Erdős stated this condition, the full question about every infinite selection is still open. I'm not a mathematician, this is my attempt at making the argument easier to follow.

chapters.title: Keep the explanation with the code

films.detail: When a codebase keeps growing, I want a way to choose where to read before asking an agent to change it. CodeMap puts saved descriptions beside recorded connections, from broad areas of a project down to a file. In this video I follow a file that prepares the map itself. The visual and agent-facing views use the same underlying code and descriptions, with different scope and detail; the connections can be incomplete.

transcript.text: Choose one finished code change to save while other agents’ unfinished edits stay in place. I use a login fix as the example, and there is a small demo you can try yourself.

films.detail: If Claude Code and Codex are working in the same project, a finished fix can end up in the same file as somebody else's unfinished change. One Checkout lets you or your agent choose the exact changes to save as a Git commit, while the other edits stay where they are. This video uses a login fix as the example, the repo also has a disposable demo you can try without touching your own project.
films.summary: Two AI coding assistants can edit the same file at the same time. I show how to save just the finished login fix as a Git commit while the other assistant’s unfinished edits stay in place.

transcript.text: How I’ve been investigating eight Erdős problems with AI, then trying to make that work understandable. Follow a result from its computer-checked proof through the papers and into the maths map.

films.detail: I've been using AI to investigate eight Erdős problems, and then trying to make that work understandable to somebody who wasn't there for the investigation. This video goes from the computer-checked proofs to the long records of what worked and failed, the shorter papers and the maths map, where you can follow one result into its paper and proof. I'm not a mathematician, this is a prototype of the preparation and explanation I think we could do with mathematicians involved. The separate #257 film goes through one argument.

transcript.text: Browse OpenAI’s maths papers alongside the reports checking them. I follow one result about pi to show why two reports can give different labels to the same omission.

films.detail: If you're interested in a mathematical result, finding the paper and then finding what other people have checked can involve a lot of searching. Plectis Atlas brings those sources together for OpenAI's maths release. In this video I look at a result about how closely fractions can approximate pi, and why two reports can use different labels while pointing out the same missing statement. The reports keep their authors and links, so you can read their actual reasons yourself.

films.label: Safety Core
films.description: A rulebook for coding agents, with a map of where each rule applies and what checks it. A saved test of a publishing request shows the checking program returning ask, then deny after one setting changes.

transcript.text: A rulebook for coding agents, with a map of where each rule applies and what checks it. A saved test of a publishing request shows the checking program returning ask, then deny after one setting changes.

films.detail: Giving an agent a rule is only part of it. I also want to see where that rule applies and what checks it. Safety Core has an editable rulebook and a map connecting the rules to folders, instructions and configured checks. The saved test sends a publishing request directly to the checking program and compares its ask and deny responses. It does not run a publishing action through Claude Code. It is still a prototype.

home.title: Plectis: projects by Will Cook
home.description: Tools and research by Will Cook for understanding the work AI produces. Explore the videos, code maps, mathematics, agent tools and their source.
home.heading: Plectis
home.lede: I'm Will Cook. These are the projects I've been building with AI.
home.orientation: Start with the introduction, or choose a project to find out more.
why: As AI gets better, it can do more work, and more complicated work. I think it's important to use those improvements to help us understand what it generates, too.

I want to see the big picture, then open the bit I don't understand. With code, that means reading a file's description and following its recorded connections back to the code. With maths, it means starting with an explanation and being able to follow it back to the paper and proof.

The agents editing my videos can read the papers and code the videos are about. I record, review the result and give feedback. I'd like to try this with researchers and lecturers who can judge the subject properly.

These videos show what I've learned to build. I'd love to put those skills to use on other problems. I'm looking for work, an internship, fellowship or funding, and I'm very open to working together. If there's a problem you think I should try, please let me know.
home.invitation: If something doesn't make sense, or you spot a mistake, please let me know. If your feedback leads to a change, I'd be happy to credit you, with your permission.

projects.name: Safety Core
projects.purpose: See where your AI assistant’s safety rules apply and what checks them.
projects.detail: A recorded test sends a publishing request directly to the checking program. Changing one setting changes its answer from ask to deny. The map links that check to the written rule.

projects.name: Demo Take
projects.purpose: Make videos from a spoken explanation, with pictures that help explain it.
projects.detail: This is what I used to make these films. I record and give feedback, and agents edit the recordings and make visuals while reading the underlying maths and code.
projects.status: Still part of my private system. There isn't a standalone public repository yet.

projects.name: Zenith
projects.purpose: Test whether AI-written tests and extra test answers help find and fix program errors.
projects.detail: One study tries AI-written tests on small programs with deliberately planted mistakes. A separate study asks whether extra test answers help an AI repair a program, then scores the selected code on later test inputs. The studies keep unsuccessful attempts as well as improvements.
projects.status: Small research studies, with limits described in the repository. The linked introduction shows an earlier version of the project; the studies report the current experiments.
